domain_label: Turlock Automotive — Market, Demand & Saturation Economics
purpose: A method for sizing and reading the Turlock independent automotive-service market: quantifying the demand base (the city vehicle parc, the ag/dairy fleet over-index, and the Hispanic/Assyrian/Portuguese/Punjabi referral channels), explaining why each of the seven sub-categories saturates at the count it does (detailing 5, mechanical 3, smog 3, tires 3, collision 2, transmission 2, parts 1), separating the regulatory and supply-chain gates from chain crowd-out and Modesto leakage, locating defensible white-space, and expressing every revenue, margin and market-size figure strictly as a labeled benchmark estimate (national per-unit benchmark x an inferred, unknown size signal) rather than as a stated fact for any named business.
assumptions: no per-business revenue dataset is supplied for these privately held independents; every dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual reported figure for any named business
the universe is the 19 verified Turlock independents in businesses.json (chains, dealer service departments, and the informal/mobile tail excluded), as of the 2026-06-30 snapshot
city/county/state figures (population, income, demographics, the $8.25 smog certificate fee, licensing regimes) are cited public facts or explicitly labeled derivations

sub-category revenue bands are published national per-unit benchmarks (per bay / per truck / per station / per car) scaled by an inferred Turlock size signal read from public offering text, years in business, and mobile-vs-shop cues, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence band
unit counts (bays, trucks, stations) are unknown for every named firm, so bands are wide on purpose and Central Valley rates push true figures toward the lower-middle of each band
Modesto (~218k, ~15 miles north) is the regional anchor that caps Turlock's high-ticket collision and specialty ceiling; national chains and dealers carry the bulk of commodity volume
the single regulated dollar fact in the sector is the $8.25 state smog certificate fee; the $30-$80/test smog price is a market band treated as estimate, not a regulated fact
exclusions: per-sub-category tooling, supplier-sourcing, and shop-floor operations detail — covered by the supply-chain KB
per-sub-category unit-economics, cost-structure and go/no-go business-model detail — covered by the business-models KB
any claim of an actual, reported, or audited dollar revenue for a named business
national/franchise chains, new-car dealer service departments, and the informal/mobile tail, which are outside the independents-only catalog
individual pricing tactics, marketing execution, or DRP contract terms for a specific operator
source_description: labeled benchmark estimates and cited public facts for the Turlock independent automotive-service market, grounded in the automotive deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its reconciliation brief, and the 19-business source dataset (businesses.json); demand sizing uses the city vehicle parc and Census demographics, sub-category revenue bands use published per-bay/per-truck/per-station benchmarks, and saturation/leakage reads use population and national establishments-per-capita figures
source_citation: U.S. Census / DataUSA (Turlock ~72,500 pop, $82,995 median HH income, ~46% Hispanic, CSU Stanislaus ~8,400 UG); bar.ca.gov (ARD/Smog/STAR licensing, $8.25 certificate fee); PartsTech/IBISWorld/Statista/BLS (revenue-per-bay and establishments-per-capita benchmarks ~5.3/10k); ATD/Transtar/Alliance-Pronto (supply chain); automotive DEEPDIVE.md, supply_ops.md, market_saturation.md, reconciled.md, businesses.json

competency_questions.question: What are the demand drivers that generate Turlock's auto-service demand, and how large is the vehicle parc as a labeled estimate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VEHICLE_PARC_DEMAND names the ~72,500 resident base in ~23-25k households and derives the ~45,000-50,000 registered-vehicle parc as households x ~1.8-2.0 vehicles, tagged estimate-not-actual with medium confidence

competency_questions.question: How does the ag/dairy/nut-belt fleet over-index Turlock's essential-service demand above a generic 73k town?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AG_FLEET_DEMAND ties the farm-truck/trailer/light-fleet parc driven hard on unimproved roads to over-indexed mechanical, tire and transmission demand and the older high-mileage cash-pay parc

competency_questions.question: How do Turlock's demographic referral channels (Hispanic, Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Punjabi) lower customer-acquisition cost and enlarge the informal tail?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMOGRAPHIC_CHANNELS ties each community to the formats and trade accounts it anchors (Mando's owner-op tire channel, ag/dairy-fleet ties) and explains the large uncataloged informal tail

competency_questions.question: How is the service-demand pool sized and what fraction do independents plausibly capture against chains and dealers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_DEMAND_POOL sizes the ~45-50k-vehicle service pool and INDEPENDENT_CAPTURE states the floor capture (chains/dealers carry the bulk of commodity volume) with its low-confidence flag and confirmation path

competency_questions.question: How is a per-sub-category benchmark revenue band built so it is an honest estimate and never a stated fact for a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBCATEGORY_REVENUE_BANDS states the benchmark-x-inferred-size-signal method, gives the seven sub-category bands, and tags every band estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: Why is a naive total-divided-by-19 average meaningless given the ~30x per-firm revenue range across sub-categories?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THIRTYX_RANGE_TRAP shows the seven sub-categories span a ~30x range from a sub-$100k solo mobile detailer to a multi-million DRP collision shop, so there is no typical auto-service business

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain 19 cataloged independents, and how does the per-10k floor relate to the all-in density?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_FLOOR_READ gives the 2.6-cataloged-independents-per-10k floor (19/72,500x10,000), contrasts it with the ~5.3/10k US norm and the ~6-10/10k all-in Turlock estimate, and explains why the floor sits below the norm

competency_questions.question: Which sub-categories are saturated/commoditized and which are thin-but-stable, by sub-category count vs gate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBCATEGORY_SATURATION_READS gives a per-sub-category count vs a crowded/adequate/thin read tied to whether a regulatory gate holds (detailing 5 commoditized, smog 3 gated, collision 2 structural, parts 1 chain-owned)

competency_questions.question: How do the regulatory and supply-chain gates cap the defensible lanes thin and stable rather than letting count expand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_GATES names the tiered gates (BAR ARD, STAR smog station + technician license, DRP + booth/frame capex for collision, Transtar/drivetrain for transmission) and ties harder gate to lower stable count

competency_questions.question: How do national chains crowd out independents in commodity lanes and collapse parts retail to a single store?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHAIN_CROWDOUT explains quick-lube/tire/parts chains absorbing transactional volume, why independent parts collapses to one store (Turlock Auto Parts), and why tire shops survive only on attached service

competency_questions.question: How does Modesto's proximity leak high-ticket collision, warranty and specialty work and thin the local count?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODESTO_LEAKAGE explains the 15-mile, ~218k anchor drawing larger collision consolidators, dealer service and import/specialty work, thinning the Turlock collision and specialty count as an estimate of behavior

competency_questions.question: How is a market go/no-go verdict reached for entering a sub-category, what gate overrides a demand-true opening, and how are the reads refreshed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_GO_NOGO composes the saturation read, white-space rank, EV erosion and the regulatory/capex gate (refusing demand-true but gated entries), and MARKET_REVIEW_LOOP defines the cadence and triggers (BAR/STAR rule change, EV-ramp data, chain footprint shift) that re-run sizing and saturation

glossary.definition: The number and age profile of vehicles on the road in a trade area; Turlock's immediate city parc is estimated at ~45,000-50,000 registered vehicles (~23-25k households x ~1.8-2.0 vehicles), the demand base auto-service keys to instead of households; a labeled estimate, not a measured count.

The honest revenue-estimation method used throughout: take a published national per-bay / per-truck / per-station / per-car benchmark and scale it by an inferred, unknown Turlock size signal (offering text, years in business, mobile-vs-shop), yielding a wide band tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level.

The per-capita saturation read 19 firms / 72,500 residents x 10,000 ~= 2.6 cataloged independent auto-service firms per 10,000 residents; explicitly a FLOOR because it excludes chains, dealers, and the informal/mobile tail, not a ceiling.

The plausible ~6-10 auto-service firms per 10,000 residents once national/franchise chains, dealer service departments and the informal tail are added back, set against the ~5.3/10k US establishments norm.

A licensing/credential barrier that caps a defensible lane: BAR ARD registration, the STAR station + smog-technician license fork, DRP gatekeeping plus booth/frame capex for collision, and drivetrain/Transtar access for transmission; the harder the gate, the lower and more stable the count.

National chains (quick-lube, Les Schwab/Big O/Costco/Walmart tire, AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA parts) owning the commodity, price-shopped lanes, which is why independent parts collapses to one store and independent tire shops survive only on attached service.

Cross-shopping to Modesto (~218k, ~15 miles north) where larger collision consolidators, more dealer service and import/specialty shops sit; high-ticket collision, warranty and specialty mechanical work leaks north, thinning the Turlock count; an estimate of behavior, not a measured study.

Heavy secondary-categorization in the catalog (E&M does mechanical+tires+parts, Balswick's does tires+repair+detail, smog-and-repair bundles both) so functional mechanical-repair capacity materially exceeds the headline primary count of 3.

The survival mechanism in commodity lanes: standalone tire or parts resale loses to chains, so independents profit from attached mechanical, alignment and brake work rather than product margin; the mini-integrated shop (E&M, Balswick's) is the durable format.

The binding honesty rule: per-business revenue is not public, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual figure for a named business; every band is a benchmark x inferred size signal carrying a method, public source basis and confidence, with the $8.25 smog certificate fee the only regulated dollar fact.

nodes.definition: Establish the demand base auto-service keys to: not households but the vehicle parc. Turlock has ~72,500 residents in roughly 23-25k households at a median household income of ~$82,995, and at ~1.8-2.0 vehicles per household the immediate city base is on the order of 45,000-50,000 registered vehicles, plus a wider south-county rural trade area. The population skews younger (median age 35), is ~46% Hispanic/Latino, and is fed by CSU Stanislaus (~8,400 undergraduates), a student/lower-income cohort driving older, higher-mileage cars that need cash-pay mechanical, tire and smog work rather than warranty dealer service. The parc figure is a labeled estimate, not a registration count.

excluded: converting the parc into a service-demand pool

pros.claim: Keying demand to the vehicle parc rather than households explains auto-service demand a population read alone cannot
pros.example: an older, higher-mileage parc supports cash-pay mechanical and smog volume a household count would miss

cons.claim: A vehicles-per-household multiplier is a national-average proxy that can misstate a specific town's parc
cons.example: a lower-income student cohort may run fewer registered vehicles than the 1.8-2.0 assumption

failure_modes: sizing demand off household count instead of the vehicle parc
treating the 45-50k parc as a measured registration figure rather than an estimate
acceptance_tests: the parc is stated as ~45,000-50,000 vehicles derived as ~23-25k households x ~1.8-2.0 vehicles, with population, income and the CSU cohort cited and tagged estimate-not-actual
revisit_triggers: a Census/ACS demographic refresh
a CSU enrollment release
a DMV registration figure becomes available

base.update_signal: a population, enrollment, or vehicle-registration figure is refreshed

nodes.definition: Capture the defining demand feature: an aging, high-mileage, ag/fleet-heavy parc. Turlock sits in a dense dairy, nut and food-processing belt, so farm trucks, trailers and light fleets driven hard on unimproved roads age faster and over-index the town on essential mechanical, tire and transmission demand relative to a generic 73k town. This is the tailwind that keeps the sector denser than a richer, newer-car suburb and partly offsets the EV/reliability erosion risk. The over-index is a qualitative structural fact; its dollar magnitude is unknown.

excluded: the demographic referral channels (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming the ag/fleet over-index explains essential-service density a generic per-capita model under-predicts
pros.example: heavy-mileage dairy and nut-belt trucks generate tire and transmission demand a suburban parc would not

cons.claim: Fleet demand is qualitative here, so it cannot be sized without fleet counts
cons.example: knowing trucks age faster does not say how many incremental repair orders that yields

failure_modes: treating ag-fleet demand as quantified when it is directional
ignoring that the over-index partly offsets the EV/reliability erosion headwind
acceptance_tests: the ag/dairy/nut-belt fleet is tied to over-indexed mechanical/tire/transmission demand and named as a tailwind on the older high-mileage parc, flagged qualitative
revisit_triggers: a county ag/dairy employment or fleet figure is published
a major processing plant opens or closes
a fleet-electrification signal appears

base.update_signal: an ag/dairy fleet or processing-employment figure changes

nodes.definition: Explain how Turlock's demographics support more small cash-pay operators than headcount alone implies, mostly enlarging the informal/uncataloged tail rather than the cataloged count. The ~46% Mexican/Hispanic base is a labor-rich, vehicle-dependent, entrepreneurial base for owner-operated tire shops (Mando's), used-car mechanical and detailing, with Spanish-language referral channels lowering customer-acquisition cost. The Assyrian (~a quarter of the city), Portuguese/Azorean (~7%) and Punjabi/South-Asian communities run high-trust in-language referral networks that support relationship-based shops and ag/dairy-fleet and trucking accounts (Portuguese-Azorean dairy ties; Punjabi ag/trucking demand on heavy-mileage fleets).

included: Assyrian/Portuguese/Punjabi trust networks and fleet accounts

pros.claim: Mapping community to channel explains why the informal tail is large and acquisition cost is low for owner-ops
pros.example: Mando's referral-driven Hispanic-community tire/wheel format wins customers without paid acquisition

cons.claim: Community share is a crude proxy for the size of the uncataloged tail, which neither upstream file could bound
cons.example: knowing the base is entrepreneurial does not say how many backyard mechanics it sustains

failure_modes: assuming demographic channels add to the cataloged count rather than the informal tail
ignoring the Portuguese/Punjabi ag-fleet trade-account demand
acceptance_tests: each of the named communities is tied to at least one channel or fleet-account effect, and the enlarged informal/uncataloged tail is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: an ancestry/demographic data refresh
a community grows or contracts via migration
an estimate of the informal tail becomes available

base.update_signal: a heritage-community share or informal-tail estimate changes

nodes.definition: Size the auto-service demand pool as a labeled read off the ~45-50k-vehicle parc plus the south-county rural trade area, recognizing it is a fixed, slow-growing volume with no tourism or commuter inflow. The pool is the demand ceiling the whole sector shares; its dollar magnitude is an estimate built from average annual repair/maintenance spend per vehicle times the parc, deliberately wide because per-vehicle spend, the rural trade-area boundary and the parc itself are all uncertain. Ag-fleet and student demand partly add to and partly sit inside this pool rather than stacking cleanly. The single best confirmation is local registration and CDTFA auto-services sales-tax data.

excluded: the independent capture fraction (its own node)

pros.claim: A transparent parc-x-spend method gives a defensible demand ceiling without quoting any business
pros.example: stating the pool as 45-50k vehicles x average annual service spend lets a reader audit the estimate end to end

cons.claim: A national per-vehicle spend average can misstate a town with an older, ag-heavy, cash-pay parc
cons.example: an older high-mileage parc could push true per-vehicle spend above the national average

failure_modes: presenting the pool as a measured figure rather than an estimate
stacking ag-fleet and student demand fully on top of the resident pool and double-counting
acceptance_tests: the pool is stated as a parc-x-per-vehicle-spend estimate over ~45-50k vehicles with a range, a confidence level and the registration/CDTFA confirmation path, tagged estimate-not-actual
revisit_triggers: a new per-vehicle service-spend benchmark
a DMV registration or parc refresh
CDTFA auto-services receipts become available

base.update_signal: a per-vehicle spend figure, parc count, or CDTFA receipt set is refreshed

nodes.definition: Estimate what fraction of the service-demand pool independents capture against national chains and dealers, and flag it as a weak number. The fixed pool is siphoned three ways: national chains own the commodity, price-shopped lanes (quick-lube, tire, chain parts); Modesto leakage takes high-ticket collision, warranty and specialty work; and dealers plus the informal/cash tail take warranty-age and low-end work. The cataloged 19 independents therefore capture only a portion of pool dollars, concentrated in cash-pay mechanical, smog, owner-op tire and detailing; the exact share is low confidence because chain and dealer volume is unmeasured locally. CDTFA split by independent vs chain is the confirmation.

included: the three-way leakage of the pool
the low-confidence flag and CDTFA confirmation
excluded: the chain-crowd-out mechanism in detail (its own node)

pros.claim: Explicitly flagging capture as the weakest link prevents a false-precision market size
pros.example: marking the independent share low-confidence stops a reader treating it as a solid figure

cons.claim: A wide flagged share limits how much downstream planning can lean on the market size
cons.example: an unmeasured chain/dealer share leaves the independent portion too wide to set a precise entry target on

failure_modes: upgrading the capture assumption to a stated fact
ignoring that chains and dealers carry the bulk of commodity and warranty volume
acceptance_tests: the capture is stated as a low-confidence portion of the pool, the three-way chain/Modesto/dealer leakage is named, and the CDTFA independent-vs-chain confirmation is given
revisit_triggers: CDTFA splits receipts by independent vs chain
a chain or dealer footprint change shifts local volume
the independent catalog count materially changes

base.update_signal: a CDTFA independent-vs-chain split or chain footprint changes

nodes.definition: Build the per-sub-category revenue bands that are the primary revenue view, every one a labeled estimate (published national per-unit benchmark x an inferred, unknown Turlock size signal), never an actual figure for a named business. Representative bands: mechanical repair small 3-4 bay $500k-$900k, established multi-bay $900k-$1.8M (~$203k/bay PartsTech); tires/wheels owner-op $400k-$900k, established tire+service $1M-$2.5M; smog test-only $150k-$300k, STAR test-and-repair $300k-$600k+; collision limited-DRP $700k-$1.5M, strong-DRP $1.5M-$3.5M; transmission specialty $500k-$1.5M; detailing solo/mobile $60k-$180k, shop+mobile w/ ceramic $120k-$350k; parts retail $500k-$1.5M. Each pairs revenue with its cost/margin reality so high gross is never read as high net.

pros.claim: Per-sub-category bands anchored to published per-unit benchmarks give a planning estimate without quoting any operator
pros.example: a mechanical band from ~$203k/bay x an inferred 3-8 bays is auditable and business-agnostic

cons.claim: Bands rest on national benchmarks and unobserved unit counts, so any single firm can sit far outside its band
cons.example: a long-standing multi-bay shop could exceed its band top while a solo mobile detailer falls below the floor

failure_modes: attaching a band to a named business as if it were that business's revenue
dropping the cost/margin pairing so a high-gross sub-category reads as high-profit
acceptance_tests: each of the seven sub-categories has a low/high band derived as a per-unit benchmark x a stated inferred size signal, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence and confirmation path, paired with its cost/margin caveat
revisit_triggers: a published per-unit benchmark updates
an observable size signal (bays, trucks, stations) is measured for a sub-category
CDTFA distribution data lands

base.update_signal: a per-unit benchmark source or measured size signal changes

nodes.definition: Make the core revenue-band math explicit and checkable for the bay-based sub-categories. The benchmark estimate is revenue = revenue_per_bay x bay_count, here demonstrated with the PartsTech ~$203,000/bay productivity benchmark: a 3-bay shop estimates ~$609,000 and an 8-bay shop estimates ~$1,624,000, bracketing the small-to-established mechanical band. Bay count is an inferred, unknown size signal for every named firm, so the output is a labeled estimate carrying the benchmark source and a wide confidence band, never a stated figure for a named business. Central Valley labor rates push true local figures toward the lower-middle of the computed range.

included: the revenue = per-bay x bay-count formula

pros.claim: An explicit, recomputable formula makes the revenue estimate auditable rather than asserted
pros.example: $203,000/bay x 3 bays = ~$609,000 can be checked by any reader against the benchmark

cons.claim: A clean formula can imply false precision when the bay count it multiplies is unknown
cons.example: a confident-looking $1.62M for 8 bays is only as good as the inferred bay count

failure_modes: presenting the formula output as a named business's revenue
using a coastal-CA per-bay benchmark without the Central-Valley lower-middle adjustment
acceptance_tests: the formula revenue = revenue_per_bay x bay_count is stated and recomputes correctly for the worked 3-bay (~$609k) and 8-bay (~$1.624M) cases at $203k/bay, with bay count flagged inferred-unknown
revisit_triggers: the per-bay benchmark is updated
a measured bay count for a sub-category becomes available

base.update_signal: the per-bay benchmark or a measured bay count changes

nodes.definition: Correct the most common misread: a naive 'total auto-service dollars / 19' is meaningless because the seven sub-categories span a ~30x revenue range per firm, from a solo mobile detailer plausibly under $100k (Adrian's, Cen-Cal, Veras profile) to an established multi-bay collision shop with strong DRP plausibly in the multi-million range (Complete Collision's 35+ years). There is no typical auto-service business in Turlock; there are seven distinct unit-economic profiles. Any single per-business average is a pool artifact, not a representative figure; the per-sub-category bands are the primary view, and CDTFA outlet-level distribution would resolve the spread.

pros.claim: Naming the 30x range stops a reader computing a single misleading per-business average
pros.example: showing a sub-$100k detailer next to a multi-million collision shop exposes the average as meaningless

cons.claim: Emphasizing the spread can make any aggregate read seem useless when sub-category bands still inform
cons.example: discarding all aggregation loses a useful count-vs-demand consistency check

failure_modes: quoting a single per-business average as representative
presenting one point estimate instead of the seven sub-category profiles
acceptance_tests: the ~30x range is stated with its low (sub-$100k mobile detailer) and high (multi-million strong-DRP collision) anchors, and the per-sub-category bands are named as the primary read
revisit_triggers: CDTFA outlet-level distribution becomes available
the capture share or per-sub-category bands are revised

base.update_signal: outlet-level revenue distribution data appears

nodes.definition: Give the saturation read as a density floor, not a ceiling: 19 independent firms / 72,500 residents x 10,000 ~= 2.6 cataloged independent auto-service firms per 10,000 residents. This 2.6/10k is a FLOOR because the catalog excludes national/franchise chains (Big O, Les Schwab-type, quick-lube, AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA, Walmart/Costco tire), dealer service departments, and the informal/mobile tail; counting those, true all-in density is plausibly 6-10/10k. The US runs ~5.3 repair/maintenance establishments per 10k. The two are not contradictory: the cataloged-independent 2.6 floor sits below the 5.3 norm because chains and dealers carry a large share of local volume, while the all-in 6-10 sits at or modestly above the norm, consistent with an older, ag-heavy, cash-pay parc.

included: the ~5.3/10k US norm and ~6-10/10k all-in estimate
why the floor sits below the norm
excluded: the gate and crowd-out mechanisms in detail

pros.claim: Framing 2.6/10k as a floor prevents a deficit misread against the 5.3 US norm
pros.example: the floor sits below the norm precisely because chains and dealers carry volume the catalog omits

cons.claim: The all-in 6-10/10k figure rests on an unbounded informal tail, so the reconciliation is itself an estimate
cons.example: without a count of chains, dealers and informal operators the all-in density is low-medium confidence

failure_modes: comparing the 2.6 cataloged-independent floor to the 5.3 all-in norm as if like-for-like
treating 2.6/10k as the true total density
acceptance_tests: the 2.6/10k floor is derived as 19/72,500x10,000, contrasted with the ~5.3/10k US norm and the ~6-10/10k all-in estimate, with the different-denominator reconciliation stated
revisit_triggers: the catalog count changes
a national establishments-per-capita update
a count of local chains/dealers/informal operators becomes available

base.update_signal: the catalog count, US norm, or all-in density estimate changes

nodes.definition: Give the per-sub-category saturation read by setting the catalog count against a crowded/adequate/thin call tied to whether a gate holds: auto detailing 5 — most crowded and commoditized, the no-BAR-license low-barrier floor, race-to-the-bottom defensible only via ceramic/fleet/dealer work; tires/wheels 3 — functionally crowded by chains, independents survive on service attach; mechanical repair 3 (+ cross-sellers) — adequately served, defensible via decades of trust (Nona's 40+ yrs); smog 3 — adequately served, regulatory and inelastic, the most defensible; collision 2 — thin and DRP-gated, structural not a gap; transmission 2 — thin specialty, high-ARO; parts retail 1 — the lane the nationals own. The pattern: high count where no barrier, low-but-stable where barriers are real, single survivor where a national category owns the lane.

included: per-sub-category catalog count and crowded/adequate/thin read
excluded: the gate mechanism detail (its own node)

pros.claim: A count-vs-read table makes each sub-category's saturation legible against its gate
pros.example: detailing 5 reads commoditized while collision 2 reads structurally thin, not a gap

cons.claim: Primary-category counts understate capacity because of heavy cross-categorization
cons.example: functional mechanical capacity exceeds the headline 3 once tire and transmission straddles are counted

failure_modes: reading a primary count as the full picture when secondary straddles shift it
reading the single parts store as white-space rather than a chain-owned lane
acceptance_tests: each of the seven sub-categories has its catalog count and a crowded/adequate/thin read tied to whether a regulatory gate holds, consistent with the floor read
revisit_triggers: a firm opens or closes in a sub-category
a gate change reclassifies a sub-category
a chain footprint shift changes a commodity read

base.update_signal: a sub-category count or anchoring demand changes

nodes.definition: Explain the tiered regulatory and supply-chain gates that cap the defensible lanes thin and stable rather than letting count expand, and why the tiering explains the count. Detailing clears no BAR gate, so count is highest and most commoditized. Smog faces a BAR ARD + STAR station license + licensed smog-technician fork (test-only vs test-and-repair), holding it to a handful of properly licensed stations. Collision faces ARD + de-facto I-CAR/ASE + air-district booth permits + DRP gatekeeping plus $50k-$150k+ booth/frame capex, structurally capping the count at 2. Transmission needs drivetrain expertise and Transtar kit access, specialty and low-volume by nature. The only regulated dollar figure is the $8.25 smog certificate fee; the inspection price itself is not BAR-regulated.

included: the $8.25 regulated fee vs unregulated inspection price
excluded: the capex figures applied to a go/no-go verdict

pros.claim: Tiering the gates explains the count better than a demand gap does
pros.example: collision's ARD+I-CAR+booth-permit+DRP stack explains a thin count of 2 as structural, not a gap

cons.claim: Gate stringency is described categorically, so the exact capex/licensing cost is a wide range
cons.example: booth+frame setup is quoted $50k-$150k+ at low confidence

failure_modes: treating the $30-$80/test smog price as a regulated fact rather than a market band
reading a thin gated count as a market gap to fill
acceptance_tests: the tiered gates are named for detailing, smog, collision and transmission, each tied to its count, and the $8.25 certificate fee is stated as the only regulated dollar figure
revisit_triggers: a BAR/STAR rule or fee change
an air-district booth-permit change
a DRP or I-CAR credential requirement shift

base.update_signal: a licensing regime, fee, or credential requirement changes

nodes.definition: Model the dominant cap on independent count: national chains own the commodity, price-shopped lanes. Quick-lube (Jiffy Lube/Valvoline), tire (Les Schwab/Big O/Costco/Walmart) and chain parts (AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA) plus online (RockAuto/Amazon) absorb the bulk of transactional volume. This is why independent parts retail collapses to a single store (Turlock Auto Parts against several national jobber storefronts and online), and why independent tire shops survive only by attaching mechanical/alignment/brake service rather than on tire-product margin. The crowd-out is the structural reason a town this size supports many service shops but only one independent parts store: the inventory-carry model needs scale the local independent channel cannot match against the nationals.

pros.claim: Naming chain crowd-out explains the single-parts-store outcome demand math alone cannot
pros.example: one independent parts store against AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA/online is crowd-out, not a demand gap

cons.claim: Chain volume is unmeasured locally, so the crowd-out share is inferred from footprint not data
cons.example: the exact transactional share chains absorb is not measured without receipts

failure_modes: reading the single parts store as white-space rather than a chain-owned lane
treating independent tire margin as tire-product margin rather than service attach
acceptance_tests: chain crowd-out is tied to the single-parts-store collapse and the tire service-attach survival, with the named chain categories listed as the volume absorbers
revisit_triggers: a national chain opens or closes a Turlock footprint
an online-parts share shift
a new independent parts entrant appears

base.update_signal: a chain footprint or online-parts share changes

nodes.definition: Model the Modesto leakage: Modesto (~218,000, ~15 miles north) hosts larger collision/consolidator shops, more dealer service, and import/specialty mechanical shops, so high-ticket collision, warranty and specialty mechanical work leaks north. This thins the Turlock-headquartered count in body and specialty repair and is part of why the local collision count is a structural 2 rather than higher, with complex jobs leaking to Modesto consolidators. The leakage is an estimate of cross-shopping behavior, not a measured leakage study; a Turlock-vs-Modesto cross-shop study would confirm its magnitude.

included: the high-ticket collision and specialty leakage

pros.claim: Naming Modesto leakage explains the thin collision/specialty count proximity creates
pros.example: complex collision jobs leak to Modesto consolidators, capping the local count at 2

cons.claim: Leakage is inferred from proximity and scale, not measured, so its magnitude is uncertain
cons.example: without a cross-shop study the share of Turlock high-ticket spend going to Modesto is unknown

failure_modes: treating the leakage estimate as a measured figure
applying high-ticket leakage logic to cash-pay essential formats Modesto does not draw
acceptance_tests: the Modesto anchor is quantified by population and distance, tied to high-ticket collision/specialty leakage and the thin collision count, and flagged as an estimate of cross-shopping behavior
revisit_triggers: a Turlock-vs-Modesto cross-shop study is done
Modesto's collision/specialty capacity expands or contracts
a new collision or specialty shop opens in Turlock

base.update_signal: Modesto cross-shop behavior or its specialty capacity changes

nodes.definition: Account for the heavy cross-categorization that makes the primary-category count understate delivered capacity. Counts use primary category as the spine, but secondary categories matter enormously: E&M does mechanical + tires + parts, Balswick's does tires + repair + detail, Countryside and Mando's do tire + mechanical, Turlock Transmissions does drivetrain + general repair, and Turlock Quick Smog & Repair bundles smog + mechanical. Functional mechanical-repair capacity therefore materially exceeds the headline primary count of 3. Saturation reads must account for this straddle; raw firm count does not, so a sub-category can look thinner than its true delivered capacity.

pros.claim: Surfacing the straddle stops a saturation read mistaking primary count for delivered capacity
pros.example: functional mechanical capacity exceeds 3 because tire and transmission shops also do general repair

cons.claim: Counting secondary capacity risks double-counting a firm across two sub-categories
cons.example: Balswick's counted under tires, repair and detail could inflate three reads at once

failure_modes: double-counting a straddling firm across its categories
ignoring straddle so a sub-category reads thinner than its true capacity
acceptance_tests: at least four straddling firms are named with their secondary categories and the functional mechanical capacity is stated as exceeding the headline 3
revisit_triggers: a firm adds or drops a secondary service line
a catalog re-categorization
a measured capacity figure appears

base.update_signal: a firm's secondary service lines or the catalog categorization changes

nodes.definition: Account for the demand peaks an annual revenue band averages away, which are a working-capital and staffing concern not visible in a flat band. A/C work spikes in Central Valley summer heat (relevant to E&M's A/C emphasis); tires spike pre-winter and with weather; detailing skews to dry/warm months and pre-sale prep; smog is steady, evenly distributed by DMV renewal cycle. Most repair/tire/smog/transmission shops run standard weekday hours, appointment- and walk-in-driven, while the ag daypart adds early-morning fleet traffic. An operator reading only an annual band will mis-plan summer A/C staffing and winter tire inventory. The peak magnitudes are directional estimates, not sized.

included: A/C summer, tire pre-winter, detailing warm-season peaks

pros.claim: Surfacing the peaks turns a flat annual band into an actionable staffing and inventory profile
pros.example: summer A/C demand is a staffing engine invisible in an annual average

cons.claim: Seasonality is hard to size without operator data, so peaks are directional not quantified
cons.example: knowing A/C spikes in summer does not say by how much without sales records

failure_modes: averaging a summer- or winter-concentrated line into a flat band and mis-sizing working capital
ignoring the ag early-morning daypart in a residential-only read
acceptance_tests: each seasonal driver (A/C summer, tire pre-winter, detailing warm-season, steady smog) is named with its peak and the working-capital/staffing risk is stated, flagged directional
revisit_triggers: a weather-pattern or climate shift changes a peak
operator sales data quantifies a peak
a daypart pattern change

base.update_signal: a seasonal peak's timing or magnitude is observed to change

nodes.definition: Distinguish the two opposite capital models that coexist in the sector, because they drive entirely different entry economics. The JIT service shops (mechanical, collision, transmission, tires) tie up capital in equipment and labor and order parts per job, with a capex ladder from mobile detailing ($5k-$15k) up through per-bay mechanical tooling and the collision booth+frame ($50k-$150k+, the heaviest in the sector). The single parts retailer ties up capital in shelf inventory instead. This is the structural reason a town this size supports many service shops but only one independent parts store: the inventory-carry model needs scale against the nationals that the JIT shops do not. Capex figures are labeled estimates with wide bands.

included: why inventory-carry supports only one store

pros.claim: Separating the two capital models explains the single-parts-store outcome and the entry capex ladder
pros.example: a $5k-$15k mobile detailing rig vs a $50k-$150k+ collision booth are opposite entry bets

cons.claim: Capex figures are wide-band estimates, so the ladder is directional not a fixed cost
cons.example: booth+frame setup swings widely with used-vs-new equipment and shop size

failure_modes: treating the collision booth capex as a fixed figure rather than a wide estimate
missing that the inventory-carry model is why parts retail is a single store
acceptance_tests: the JIT-equipment vs inventory-carry split is stated, the capex ladder from mobile ($5k-$15k) to collision ($50k-$150k+) is given as labeled estimates, and the single-parts-store consequence is named
revisit_triggers: an equipment or commercial-rent cost change
a startup-capex benchmark update
a new inventory-carry entrant appears

base.update_signal: an equipment, rent, or startup-capex figure changes

nodes.definition: Surface the unquantified erosion risk: improving vehicle reliability and the early edge of EV adoption (fewer oil changes, no smog for BEVs, no multi-speed transmission) slowly erode the demand pool, most directly threatening smog (BEVs exempt) and transmission (none on a BEV). The local EV timeline is unknown, so this is a directional headwind, not a sized erosion. It is offset by the ag-fleet/older-parc tailwind that keeps the sector denser than a richer, newer-car suburb. The net effect on count and bands is uncertain, but smog and transmission carry the most downside and should be read as slowly-shrinking-pool lanes rather than growth lanes.

included: the EV/reliability erosion of smog and transmission demand

pros.claim: Flagging EV erosion stops smog and transmission being read as durable growth lanes
pros.example: BEVs are smog-exempt and have no multi-speed transmission, slowly shrinking both pools

cons.claim: The local EV timeline is unknown, so the erosion is directional and could be slow
cons.example: an older ag-heavy parc may electrify far slower than the national average, muting the risk

failure_modes: sizing the EV erosion as if the local timeline were known
ignoring the ag-fleet/older-parc tailwind that offsets it
acceptance_tests: the EV/reliability erosion is tied specifically to smog and transmission, flagged unknown-local-timeline, and the ag-fleet offset is named
revisit_triggers: a local EV adoption or registration figure appears
a BAR smog-exemption rule change
a transmission-reliability or EV-mix signal

base.update_signal: a local EV-adoption or smog-exemption signal appears

nodes.definition: Locate and rank the defensible white-space — lanes where both demand and operations permit entry — and mark each viable only after the regulatory/capex gate clears. Ranked: (1) fleet/ag-vehicle specialty service — heavy-mileage trucks, trailers and diesel tied to the dairy/nut belt, real demand under-served by the generalist catalog; (2) mobile mechanical — extending the low-capex come-to-customer detailing playbook to repair; (3) EV-readiness — high-voltage service and tires/brakes for heavier EVs, near-unserved locally as the parc slowly electrifies. Commodity detailing is explicitly NOT white-space: it is easy to enter and therefore unrewarding at the price-competed tier against a large informal tail. The binding constraint on the real openings is often the gate, not demand.

excluded: the per-decision go/no-go verdict (its own node)

pros.claim: Ranking white-space by demand and feasibility prevents recommending an un-rewarding commodity lane
pros.example: fleet/ag specialty ranks first on real under-served demand while commodity detailing is flagged not white-space

cons.claim: A ranked list can read as a recommendation when each opening still needs an operator's feasibility check
cons.example: EV-readiness ranks as genuine white-space but depends on an uncertain local EV timeline

failure_modes: listing commodity detailing as white-space because it is easy to enter
ranking an opening on demand alone without the gate or EV-timeline caveat
acceptance_tests: at least three white-space openings are ranked, each with its demand basis and a gate/feasibility qualifier, and commodity detailing is explicitly excluded as not white-space
revisit_triggers: a white-space opening is entered locally
a demand or EV-timeline shift changes an opening
a gate or capex change alters feasibility

base.update_signal: a white-space opening is entered or its demand/gate changes

nodes.definition: Define the entry gate that can override a demand-true opening, the barrier the demand view alone misses. A new body shop's real obstacle is landing insurer DRP relationships and financing $50k-$150k+ of booth/frame capex, plus ARD registration and de-facto I-CAR/ASE credentials and air-district booth permits — not finding accident volume. A new smog station's obstacle is meeting STAR performance standards and securing a licensed inspector, not finding cars. A mobile mechanical entrant still needs ARD registration and hazmat-handling compliance. These are cited public licensing facts (the $8.25 certificate fee aside, the costs are estimates). The market read must treat 'low-capital' and 'easy white space' as demand-true but gated: the binding constraint is often permitting and credentialed labor, not ingredient cost.

pros.claim: Foregrounding the gate prevents a demand-true opening from being read as actually enterable
pros.example: a new body shop looks open on accident volume until the DRP + $50k-$150k+ booth wall is priced in

cons.claim: Licensing/capex costs vary and DRP access is insurer-specific, so the figure is a range not a fixed cost
cons.example: DRP relationships and booth capex swing widely, so the wall is a band

failure_modes: recommending a collision or smog opening without pricing the gate
treating credentialed labor (smog inspector, I-CAR tech) as a cost line rather than a hiring bottleneck
acceptance_tests: the collision DRP+booth wall, the smog STAR+inspector gate, and the mobile-mechanical ARD/hazmat gate are each stated and applied as an override on the relevant white-space openings
revisit_triggers: a BAR/STAR/ARD fee or rule change
an air-district booth-permit change
a DRP access or credentialed-labor availability shift

base.update_signal: a permit, license, credential, or capex figure or availability changes

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every dollar figure: per-business revenue is not public for these privately held independents, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business. Every sub-category band is a labeled benchmark estimate (national per-unit benchmark x an inferred, unknown size signal) tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path; every high-gross band is paired with its thin-net-margin caveat; the $8.25 smog certificate fee is the only regulated dollar fact, while the $30-$80/test price is a market estimate; structural facts (demographics, licensing regimes) are cited, and supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference unless cited. This guardrail governs how all the sizing and band nodes may be expressed.

included: the high-gross/thin-net pairing and supplier-inference caveat

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail keeps every downstream number honest and auditable
pros.example: tagging every sub-category band estimate-not-actual prevents any figure being read as an audited business revenue

cons.claim: Heavy labeling can make the analysis read as hedged and lower its perceived usefulness
cons.example: a reader wanting a single revenue number is frustrated by a wide band tagged low-confidence

failure_modes: letting a sub-category band attach to a named business as that business's revenue
stating the $30-$80/test smog price as a regulated fact rather than a market estimate
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure in any node is a labeled estimate or a cited public fact, no named-business actual revenue appears, the $8.25 fee is the only regulated dollar fact, and each high-gross band carries its thin-net caveat
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a dollar figure
a public-fact source is added or updated
an actual revenue datum (e.g., CDTFA) becomes available to replace an estimate

base.update_signal: a new dollar figure is introduced or an actual datum becomes available

nodes.definition: Produce the market go/no-go verdict for entering a given sub-category, composing the saturation read, the white-space rank, the chain crowd-out, the EV erosion trajectory and the regulatory/capex gate into one decision. The merged rule: do not add a sixth detailer (commoditized, large informal tail), a second independent parts store (chain-owned lane), or fight the nationals on tire-product margin; the defensible headroom is fleet/ag specialty service, mobile mechanical and EV-readiness, each viable only after clearing the ARD/STAR/DRP and capex gate. A demand-true opening that fails the gate is a no-go until the gate clears, and smog/transmission entries must be discounted for EV erosion. Every revenue rationale in the verdict is expressed as a labeled estimate under the honesty guardrail.

pros.claim: Composing all reads into one verdict gives an actionable enter/avoid call instead of scattered signals
pros.example: the verdict says no to a sixth detailer but yes to fleet/ag specialty once the ARD gate is cleared

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a sub-category whose demand and gate point opposite ways
cons.example: EV-readiness has demand headroom yet needs an EV-timeline and capex pass before a clean yes

failure_modes: issuing a yes on demand headroom while ignoring an unmet gate
recommending a smog or transmission entry without discounting EV erosion
acceptance_tests: the verdict for a proposed sub-category combines its saturation read, white-space rank, crowd-out, EV trajectory and gate status, refuses any demand-true but gated entry, and names the do-not-add lanes
revisit_triggers: a saturation read, trajectory, crowd-out, or gate feeding the verdict changes
a previously gated opening clears its gate

base.update_signal: a saturation, trajectory, crowd-out, or gate input to the verdict changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the market reads current. A fixed refresh cadence (re-run on each major data release) plus material-change triggers — new CDTFA / auto-services sales-tax or registration data (which collapse pool size, capture share and per-firm distribution at once), a Census/ACS demographic refresh, a BAR/STAR licensing-rule or fee change, a local EV-adoption signal, a national chain footprint shift, or a major processing plant opening or closing — that send the analysis back through SERVICE_DEMAND_POOL and the saturation reads. Without this loop the 2026-06-30 snapshot silently goes stale as the EV ramp erodes smog/transmission, chains shift the commodity lanes, and Modesto's competitive gravity moves.

included: re-entry into pool sizing and saturation

pros.claim: A trigger list with the CDTFA/registration confirmation keeps the lowest-confidence numbers on a path to resolution
pros.example: the arrival of auto-services sales-tax data fires the loop and replaces the pool and capture estimates at once

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the reads without new signal, since most inputs update only annually
cons.example: re-sizing the pool monthly when registration and Census counts move only yearly wastes effort

failure_modes: no cadence set so the snapshot ages silently past its EV and chain assumptions
ignoring a fired trigger (new CDTFA/registration data) and continuing on stale estimates
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and an explicit material-change trigger list exist, each routing back to SERVICE_DEMAND_POOL and the saturation reads, with CDTFA/registration named as the highest-leverage trigger
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs actually update

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

edges.why_related: the ag/fleet over-index is a refinement of the broad vehicle-parc base into the heavy-mileage segment
the demographic referral channels resolve the resident base into community-specific demand and informal tail
the service-demand pool is sized from the vehicle parc established in the demand base
the independent capture share is a fraction of the service-demand pool just sized
per-sub-category bands are cross-checked against the total pool they must sit within
the per-bay formula is the explicit math behind the bay-based sub-category bands
the meaningless per-business average would be the captured pool divided by the firm count
the ~30x range that voids the average is read off the seven per-sub-category bands
the density floor read uses the independents-only catalog that capture is computed over
per-sub-category reads decompose the overall floor into sub-category-by-sub-category calls
the tiered gates explain the specific counts the floor read aggregates
chain crowd-out is the dominant cap that holds the cataloged-independent floor below the US norm
Modesto leakage is one of the forces thinning the count the floor read captures
the harder a sub-category's gate, the lower and more stable its saturation count
chain crowd-out causally collapses parts retail to one store and commoditizes tire/detailing reads
Modesto leakage causally thins the collision and specialty saturation reads
the straddle correction adjusts the per-sub-category reads for under-counted functional capacity
the ag early-morning fleet daypart is a seasonality factor inherited from the fleet demand node
the capex ladder pairs with the gate stringency to set per-sub-category entry economics
the JIT-vs-inventory capital split is read alongside the sub-category revenue bands
the EV erosion overlay reads the smog and transmission saturation status before judging the headwind
white-space is the under-served end of the per-sub-category saturation reads
the gate qualifier on each white-space opening comes from the regulatory-gate map
EV-readiness ranks as white-space precisely because of the erosion trajectory the EV node defines
the entry gate is applied as an override on each ranked white-space opening
demand ranks an opening attractive while the DRP/STAR/capex gate can make it un-enterable, pulling opposite ways
edges.resolution_rule: a demand-true opening is a no-go until its regulatory/capex gate (ARD/STAR for smog, DRP+booth for collision, hazmat/ARD for mobile) clears; demand never overrides an unmet gate

edges.why_related: the capex side of the entry gate is read off the two-capital-model ladder
the guardrail governs how the per-sub-category bands may be expressed and labeled
the guardrail enforces the estimate-not-actual labeling on the capture and pool figures
the go/no-go verdict consumes the per-sub-category saturation read
the verdict elevates the highest-ranked white-space openings as candidate yeses
the verdict applies the entry gate as the override that turns a demand-true yes into a no
the verdict must express any revenue rationale as a labeled estimate under the guardrail
the review loop watches the inputs to the verdict and re-triggers it when they change
a new CDTFA/registration or Census release sends the analysis back to re-size the pool
a plant open/close, chain shift or EV signal re-runs the saturation reads

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_entry_gate
conflict_axes.description: A sub-category can be demand-true white space yet be walled off by DRP, STAR licensing or booth/frame capex, so the demand and feasibility views point opposite ways.
poles: block on the unmet entry gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true opening as a no-go until its regulatory/capex gate clears; demand never overrides permitting or credentialed labor

conflict_axes.name: primary_count_vs_straddle_capacity
conflict_axes.description: The primary-category count understates delivered capacity because tire, transmission and smog shops also do general mechanical, so the headline count and functional capacity disagree.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use primary category as the spine but adjust the saturation read for secondary-category straddle without double-counting a firm

conflict_axes.name: cataloged_floor_vs_all_in_density
conflict_axes.description: The 2.6/10k cataloged-independent floor and the ~6-10/10k all-in density use different denominators and can be read as contradicting the ~5.3/10k US norm.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the 2.6 floor is independents-only and sits below the norm by design; reconcile only against the all-in figure that adds chains, dealers and the informal tail

conflict_axes.name: gate_protection_vs_chain_crowdout
conflict_axes.description: A regulatory gate protects a thin lane while chain crowd-out caps an ungated lane, two different mechanisms that both lower count but point to opposite entry advice.
poles: count capped by the regulatory gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gated lanes are thin-but-defensible once cleared; chain-crowded lanes are thin-and-unrewarding; apply each mechanism to the lane it governs

conflict_axes.name: ag_fleet_tailwind_vs_ev_erosion
conflict_axes.description: The ag-fleet/older-parc tailwind keeps the sector dense while EV adoption and rising reliability erode smog and transmission demand, pulling the trajectory opposite ways.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the tailwind sustains essential mechanical/tire demand; the erosion most threatens smog and transmission; net them per sub-category, not sector-wide

conflict_axes.name: annual_band_vs_seasonal_concentration
conflict_axes.description: A flat annual revenue band averages away the A/C-summer, tire-pre-winter and detailing warm-season peaks that drive working-capital and staffing risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the annual band with the sub-category's seasonal/daypart profile before any cash-flow or staffing read

conflict_axes.name: regulated_fee_vs_market_price
conflict_axes.description: The $8.25 smog certificate fee is regulated fact while the $30-$80/test price is a market band; conflating them states a market price as a regulated fact.
poles: treat the $30-$80 test price as regulated
treat only the $8.25 fee as regulated
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the $8.25 certificate fee as the only regulated dollar figure and the $30-$80 price as a market estimate

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous estimate-not-actual labeling protects honesty but can make the analysis read as too hedged to act on.
poles: label every figure as an estimate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure but pair it with a confidence and a confirmation path so the read stays actionable without overclaiming a named-business revenue

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_stability_vs_trend_drift
conflict_axes.description: The 19-count reads as stable, but the EV ramp, chain footprint shifts and Modesto's competitive gravity are moving the underlying forces.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the 2026-06-30 snapshot as a dated baseline but let the review loop, not assumption, decide when drift has moved the equilibrium

edge_cases.description: A reader divides total auto-service dollars by 19 and quotes a per-business average
edge_cases.trigger: the pool dollars are divided by the firm count and quoted as typical
edge_cases.mitigation: name the ~30x per-firm range and present the seven sub-category profiles as the primary read instead of any average

edge_cases.description: A sub-category band is attached to a named business as if it were that business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: a per-sub-category estimate is quoted next to a specific operator's name
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every band sub-category-level and estimate-not-actual; never bind a dollar figure to a named business as fact

edge_cases.description: The $30-$80/test smog price is stated as a BAR-regulated fact
edge_cases.trigger: the market inspection price is presented as regulated alongside the certificate fee
edge_cases.mitigation: carry only the $8.25 certificate fee as regulated; label the $30-$80 price a competitive market estimate

edge_cases.description: A new body-shop opening is recommended without pricing the DRP + booth/frame wall
edge_cases.trigger: collision white-space is judged on accident volume alone
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the DRP relationship + $50k-$150k+ booth/frame capex + I-CAR/ASE gate as an override before any collision yes

edge_cases.description: The single independent parts store is read as white-space to fill
edge_cases.trigger: parts retail count of 1 is treated as an under-served gap
edge_cases.mitigation: classify the single store as a chain-owned lane (AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA/online), not white-space; a second store is a structural loser

edge_cases.description: Smog or transmission is read as a durable growth lane
edge_cases.trigger: regulatory inelasticity or specialty status is conflated with a growing pool
edge_cases.mitigation: classify smog and transmission as defensible but slowly-shrinking under EV erosion, not growth lanes

edge_cases.description: An A/C-summer or tire-winter line is sized on a flat annual band
edge_cases.trigger: an annual revenue band is used for staffing or working-capital planning without the seasonal profile
edge_cases.mitigation: overlay the sub-category's A/C-summer, tire-pre-winter or detailing warm-season peak before any cash-flow read

edge_cases.description: Functional mechanical capacity is read off the headline primary count of 3
edge_cases.trigger: the primary mechanical count is treated as the full delivered capacity
edge_cases.mitigation: count secondary-category straddles (E&M, Balswick's, Countryside, Mando's, Turlock Transmissions, Quick Smog) so capacity exceeds 3 without double-counting

edge_cases.description: Turlock's count is read as a deficit by comparing the 2.6 floor to the 5.3 US norm
edge_cases.trigger: the cataloged-independent floor is compared to the all-in norm as like-for-like
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile denominators: the 2.6 floor is independents-only and the ~6-10/10k all-in figure sits at or above the norm

edge_cases.description: A supplier (PPG, LKQ, ATD, Transtar) is named as a confirmed contract for a specific shop
edge_cases.trigger: a representative-inference supplier link is stated as a confirmed relationship
edge_cases.mitigation: treat supplier-to-named-business links as representative inference unless a cited source states the relationship

edge_cases.description: CDTFA / registration data arrives and contradicts the estimated pool and capture share
edge_cases.trigger: measured auto-services receipts or registration counts become available
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the review loop, replace the pool/capture/distribution estimates with the measured figures, and re-derive the per-firm read

workflow.description: Record the resident base, income and CSU cohort and derive the ~45-50k vehicle parc
workflow.gate: the parc is stated as ~45-50k vehicles from ~23-25k households x ~1.8-2.0 vehicles with cited magnitudes

workflow.action: Map ag-fleet over-index and demographic channels
workflow.description: Tie the dairy/nut-belt fleet and the heritage referral channels to over-indexed essential demand and the informal tail
workflow.gate: the ag-fleet over-index and each community channel are named with their demand effect

workflow.description: Derive the pool as parc x per-vehicle service spend with range, confidence and the registration/CDTFA confirmation path
workflow.gate: the pool is stated estimate-not-actual with derivation, range and confirmation path

workflow.action: Estimate independent capture and flag it
workflow.description: State the low-confidence independent share and the three-way chain/Modesto/dealer leakage
workflow.gate: the capture is low-confidence-flagged with the leakage breakdown and CDTFA confirmation

workflow.description: Derive each band as a per-unit benchmark x an inferred size signal, paired with its cost/margin caveat, with the per-bay math made explicit
workflow.gate: every band is estimate-not-actual with a size signal, confidence and cost/margin pairing and the per-bay formula recomputes

workflow.description: Show the ~30x per-firm range and that there is no typical auto-service business
workflow.gate: the ~30x range is stated with its low and high anchors and the sub-category bands named primary

workflow.action: Read the density floor and per-sub-category saturation
workflow.description: Set the 2.6/10k floor against the norm and each sub-category count against a crowded/adequate/thin read
workflow.gate: the floor is derived and each of the seven sub-categories has a count and a gate-tied read

workflow.action: Attribute the count to gates, crowd-out and leakage
workflow.description: Name the tiered gates, the chain crowd-out and the Modesto leakage that set each count
workflow.gate: the tiered gates, chain crowd-out and Modesto leakage are each tied to the counts they explain

workflow.action: Overlay straddle, seasonality, capital models and EV erosion
workflow.description: Adjust for cross-category straddle and seasonal dayparts, state the two capital models, and flag the EV erosion on smog/transmission
workflow.gate: straddle, seasonality, the JIT-vs-inventory split and the EV erosion on smog/transmission are each stated

workflow.action: Rank white-space and apply the entry gate
workflow.description: Order fleet/ag, mobile mechanical and EV-readiness and mark each viable only after the gate clears
workflow.gate: three+ openings are ranked with a demand basis and a gate qualifier, commodity detailing excluded

workflow.action: Compose the go/no-go verdict and set the review loop
workflow.description: Combine saturation, white-space, crowd-out, EV trajectory and the gate into an enter/avoid call, then define the refresh cadence and triggers
workflow.gate: the verdict refuses any demand-true but gated entry and a trigger list routes back to pool sizing and saturation

dominance_rules.rule: The revenue-honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive number
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public for these independents, so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named business's revenue or a single market number
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labeled estimate (benchmark x inferred size signal) plus confidence and confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The entry gate dominates a demand-true white-space opening
dominance_rules.rationale: DRP, STAR licensing and booth/frame capex can make a high-demand lane un-enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a white-space opening is judged attractive on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: mark it a no-go until the ARD/STAR/DRP and capex gate clears

dominance_rules.rule: The sub-category profile dominates the per-business average
dominance_rules.rationale: the ~30x range means no single average is representative
dominance_rules.trigger: a per-business average is used to characterize a typical operator
dominance_rules.action: replace it with the relevant sub-category band and name the seven distinct profiles

dominance_rules.rule: Chain crowd-out dominates a demand-gap read of an ungated commodity lane
dominance_rules.rationale: the single parts store and crowded tire lane reflect chain ownership, not a fillable gap
dominance_rules.trigger: a thin ungated lane is read as white-space to enter
dominance_rules.action: classify the lane as chain-owned and refuse a second-store or tire-margin entry

dominance_rules.rule: The regulatory gate dominates a count-gap read of a thin gated lane
dominance_rules.rationale: collision 2 and transmission 2 are structural gate outcomes, not market gaps
dominance_rules.trigger: a thin gated count is read as an under-served gap
dominance_rules.action: attribute the thin count to the gate and treat it as defensible-once-cleared, not open

dominance_rules.rule: The seasonal/daypart profile dominates the annual band for cash-flow reads
dominance_rules.rationale: a flat annual band hides the A/C-summer and tire-winter peaks that drive working-capital risk
dominance_rules.trigger: an annual band is used for a cash-flow or staffing decision
dominance_rules.action: overlay the sub-category's seasonal/daypart profile before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The $8.25 certificate fee dominates the $30-$80 market price as the regulated fact
dominance_rules.rationale: only the certificate fee is BAR-regulated; the inspection price is a market band
dominance_rules.trigger: the smog test price is cited as a regulated fact
dominance_rules.action: carry $8.25 as the regulated fee and the $30-$80 price as a labeled market estimate

dominance_rules.rule: Per-10k denominator alignment dominates a raw floor-vs-norm comparison
dominance_rules.rationale: comparing the 2.6 cataloged-independent floor to the 5.3 all-in norm misleads
dominance_rules.trigger: the floor is compared to the US norm as like-for-like
dominance_rules.action: reconcile denominators and use the ~6-10/10k all-in figure against the norm

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the capture share or a benchmark band carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the confirmation source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size the service-demand pool before estimating independent capture or per-sub-category bands
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deriving capture and bands against a pool that later moves, forcing a full re-derivation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every dollar figure estimate-not-actual at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read saturation off primary category, noting secondary straddles, before counting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: double-counted straddle firms inflating a saturation read that must be re-tallied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the entry gate while ranking white-space, not after recommending it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a collision or smog opening that the DRP/STAR/capex gate then voids

anti_rework_rules.rule: Separate the cataloged-independent floor from the all-in density before any norm comparison
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a deficit conclusion that must be redone once the denominators are aligned

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the seasonal/daypart profile to a sub-category's band when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a flat-band staffing plan that must be reworked once the A/C-summer and tire-winter peaks are surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Flag the capture share low-confidence and carry the chain/Modesto/dealer leakage the first time it is used
anti_rework_rules.prevents: every downstream market size inheriting an unflagged assumption that must be re-marked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry the $8.25-fact vs $30-$80-estimate distinction on every smog dollar figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to correct smog prices already published as regulated facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Discount smog and transmission for EV erosion when first reading their saturation, not at the verdict
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a growth-lane misread that must be unwound once the EV headwind is applied

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA / auto-services sales-tax or DMV registration data becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the pool, capture share and per-firm distribution estimates with measured figures and re-derive the bands

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Census/ACS demographic or CSU enrollment refresh lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the demand base and ag-fleet/demographic channels and re-size the pool

iteration_protocol.trigger: a BAR/STAR licensing rule, fee, or credential requirement changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the regulatory and entry gate and re-issue any affected go/no-go verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a national chain opens or closes a Turlock footprint or online-parts share shifts
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the crowd-out read and the affected commodity saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a local EV-adoption signal or smog-exemption rule change appears
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight the EV erosion on smog/transmission and re-rank white-space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a firm opens or closes in a sub-category
iteration_protocol.action: re-tally the saturation reads and the straddle-adjusted capacity

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Turlock-vs-Modesto cross-shop study or Modesto capacity change appears
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the Modesto leakage and the thin collision/specialty reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: an equipment, rent, or startup-capex benchmark moves
iteration_protocol.action: re-pair the revenue bands and entry gate with refreshed capital reality

priority_rationale: The vehicle-parc base, ag-fleet over-index and demographic channels are foundational because pool sizing, saturation and white-space all read from them; pool sizing and capture precede the per-sub-category bands, the per-bay formula and the no-typical-business correction they constrain; the density floor, gates, chain crowd-out and Modesto leakage build on the demand and band layers to attribute the count; straddle, seasonality, capital models and EV erosion overlay the saturation reads; the revenue-honesty guardrail governs every dollar expression; and the go/no-go verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a decision and a self-correcting refresh.
